quizzes.stem: A project holds `.claude/commands/deploy.md`, and a teammate then adds `.claude/skills/deploy/SKILL.md`. What does `/deploy` run?

options.a: The command, because it was in the project first of the two
options.b: Both in turn, since the two files create the same command
options.c: The skill, since it takes precedence over the older format
options.d: Neither, until one of the two files is renamed or removed

explanation.c: The product merged the two formats and gives the skill precedence over a command file of the same name, whichever file came first.
explanation.a: Ruled out because "A skill beats a command file of the same name", and the order of arrival plays no part.
explanation.b: Ruled out because "When a skill and a command file share a name, the skill runs", so one definition answers the name and not both.
explanation.d: Ruled out because the shared name needs no repair: the skill runs at once, and "Existing command files keep working" without being renamed or removed.

quizzes.stem: A session starts at a monorepo's root, and a skill sits in `packages/api/.claude/skills/`. So far Claude has worked only inside `docs/`. When can the skill first be used?

options.a: As soon as a file under `packages/api` is read or edited
options.b: Already, since it loaded at startup with the root skills
options.c: Never, since only the start folder and its parents are searched
options.d: Only after a new session is started inside `packages/api`

explanation.a: A skill below the start folder is not found at launch; it loads when Claude first works with a file in that folder, which has not happened yet.
explanation.b: Ruled out because the launch search covers "the directory where you start and from every parent up to the repository root", and `packages/api` is neither.
explanation.c: Ruled out because "a skill in a folder below the start directory loads" later, when a file there is first used.
explanation.d: Ruled out because the skill loads "the first time Claude reads or edits a file in that subdirectory", inside the running session, and then the skills "stay available for the rest of the session".

quizzes.stem: A skill's header lists `allowed-tools: Read Grep`, and its author expects editing to be impossible while the skill is active. What actually happens?

options.a: Editing is removed from the available tools until the next message
options.b: Editing is refused because only the two listed tools are permitted
options.c: Editing runs without any prompt because the skill vouches for it
options.d: Changing files remains allowed under the usual permission settings

explanation.d: The field pre-approves and restricts nothing.
explanation.a: Ruled out because removal belongs to the other field, which removes tools "from Claude's available pool while this skill is active".
explanation.b: Ruled out because the field "does not restrict which tools are available: every tool remains callable".
explanation.c: Ruled out because "your permission settings still govern tools that are not listed".

quizzes.stem: A skill's text says only 'Use these naming conventions for new endpoints', and its header sets `context: fork`. What comes of invoking it?

options.a: A subagent starts with a copy of the conversation and applies the conventions to it
options.b: A subagent starts with those guidelines as its whole prompt and no job to carry out
options.c: A subagent starts with the conventions and applies them to the endpoint files
options.d: A subagent starts with an empty prompt, since the body holds no instruction

explanation.b: The fork hands the body to a new subagent as its prompt, and a line of conventions names no endpoint and no job, so the subagent has nothing to carry out.
explanation.a: Ruled out because the name misleads and "this is not a fork of the conversation": the subagent "doesn't see your conversation history".
explanation.c: Ruled out because a body of guidelines "gives the subagent no task", so nothing tells it to change any file.
explanation.d: Ruled out because the setting "gives it the skill content as its prompt", so the conventions are the prompt and it is not empty.

quizzes.stem: Scenario S2, code generation with Claude Code. A team uses Claude Code for refactoring and tests. A skill explains how an old billing system works. Developers who pick it from the slash menu get a page of notes and nothing done, yet Claude must keep drawing on it during billing refactors. Which header line fits?

explanation.c: It hides the skill from the person and leaves it available to Claude, which suits background knowledge.
explanation.a: Ruled out because it does the opposite, so that only the person starts it and "the full skill loads only when you invoke it".
explanation.b: Ruled out because the hint "only shows the expected shape in autocomplete", so the skill stays in the menu for the developers to pick.
explanation.d: Ruled out because `context: fork` "only makes sense for skills with explicit instructions", so a fork would run a background note as a task with nothing to do.

quizzes.stem: Scenario S2, code generation with Claude Code. A team uses Claude Code for refactoring and tests. The team's review skill must be unable to change files for the turn that runs it. Which header line does that?

options.c: `allowed-tools: Bash(gh pr view *) Bash(gh pr diff *)`

explanation.b: A bare name in the removal field takes the tool out of the pool while the skill is active.
explanation.a: Ruled out because a bare name "removes the tool from Claude's context entirely", only the tool it names, so taking away the shell leaves Edit and Write in the pool.
explanation.c: Ruled out because that field is a pre-approval, so with it "Edit and Write stay callable" and the permission settings decide.
explanation.d: Ruled out because "only a bare name removes a tool", so the scoped entry leaves editing in place.

quizzes.stem: Scenario S2, code generation with Claude Code. A team uses Claude Code for refactoring and tests. A command text reads 'Summarise the commits by $ARGUMENTS since yesterday', and a developer runs `/standup ana`. What does Claude receive?

options.a: The sentence with `$ARGUMENTS` left as is, as no name was declared
options.b: The sentence with a blank where the name belongs
options.c: The sentence unchanged, followed by a line `ARGUMENTS: ana`
options.d: The sentence with the name filled in and nothing appended

explanation.d: The placeholder received the input, so it is substituted and nothing is added.
explanation.a: Ruled out because `$ARGUMENTS` needs no declaration and takes "All arguments, as typed", so it is replaced in the text.
explanation.b: Ruled out because a blank arises only for a named placeholder without an argument, since an indexed one "stays in the content unchanged", and here the input is given.
explanation.c: Ruled out because the extra line appears only when "no placeholder receives them", and `$ARGUMENTS` is a placeholder that received the name.
